recommendedTitle: Use verified client identity for public rate limits
summary: The current rate key uses leftmost X-Forwarded-For. Actual ingress and spoof resistance must be verified before changing the trusted identity boundary.
currentBehavior: clientRateLimitKey still reads the leftmost forwarded address and falls back to unknown. Official Railway employee guidance states its HTTP proxy sets and overwrites X-Real-IP and prevents direct access through that arrangement; stable peer CIDRs are not published. This is provider guidance, not proof of the actual CallCaster ingress. An additional proxy, direct/local request identity and forged-header controls remain unverified.
rootCause: The rate-limit helper receives a Request without a verified transport identity and trusts forwarded input without an established CallCaster proxy boundary.
resolution: Inspect the real CallCaster public ingress and direct/local server arrangement. Prove overwrite or append behavior using actual forged-header and valid-client controls, then implement the verified transport rule. Preserve PostgreSQL windows and authenticated-user limits. Do not infer trust from X-Railway-Edge or an undocumented private CIDR.
missingTests: Actual transport/proxy arrangement with client-supplied X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP, valid clients, IPv4/IPv6, missing/malformed headers and stable local peer identity.
acceptanceCriteria: Derive public auth rate-limit identity from a verified transport/proxy boundary. A client cannot obtain a fresh bucket by varying the leftmost X-Forwarded-For or any other untrusted identity header.
Document the actual public ingress and trusted-hop rule, including direct/local requests and additional proxies where present.

Keep a real permitted-client control, IPv4/IPv6 controls and missing/malformed-header controls. Headerless local requests must not all share one unknown identity, and a fresh random key per request is not an acceptable fallback.
Test the actual production request arrangement, not only Request fixtures that set the supposed trusted header. Record what overwrites or appends each address field.
Preserve the existing distributed PostgreSQL window contract and authenticated user-based write limits.
Full npm run ci:local and final remote gates pass; deployed forged-header controls prove the rule before release promotion.
trackerRecommendation: Unassigned native child of #2099. Required CallCaster ingress proof remains; primary provider guidance was added to the issue without claiming acceptance.
